slides.prompt: Find the missing sentence. A story lost one sentence. UASA: put 8 back. Learn 3 skills.
slides.alt: A puzzle piece outline for the missing sentence
slides.hint: Ask: what story is this? What is missing?
slides.notes: ORIENT (~5 min, whole class, no partner talk). Sayable: a comic lost a few sentences; detectives put them back. Correct the one-word myth: not one word, one whole sentence. Practices today use short stories with 2 choices; official UASA has 8 gaps (notes.md). Tue 8 Sep, sl_t3, 60 min.

slides.prompt: Bridge the gap. Read before AND after.
items: Read the sentence BEFORE the gap.
Read the sentence AFTER the gap.
Choose the one joining BOTH sides.
slides.notes: MODEL Skill 1 (~6 min). Sayable model (teacher talk): Lina baked cookies in the morning, gap, she gave every cookie to neighbours. Bridge example: she put the hot cookies in a red box. Counter one-side reading: one side is not enough, a bridge touches both sides. Mime a bridge with hands.

options: Last Saturday she baked a delicious chocolate cake.
She dislikes going to the busy supermarket.
slides.answer: Last Saturday she baked a delicious chocolate cake.
slides.feedback: A joins baking to eating. B misses both sides.
slides.hint: Point at baked. Point at ate. Which choice names the baked food eaten?
slides.notes: PRACTISE Skill 1 (~6 min: 1 min silent, 30 s whisper, reveal why). Most pick A; B-choices signal one-side reading. Follow-up: what word joins before (cake/desserts)? What joins after (slice/cake)? Long sentence is not the rule; joins-both-sides is.

slides.prompt: Follow the pronoun. Who does it point to?
items: he = a boy or man; she = a girl or woman.
it = one thing; they = more than one.
Rule: it points to the sentence BEFORE.
Danial bought a kite. It flew high.
slides.notes: MODEL Skill 2 (~6 min). Choral substitution: It = the kite. Sayable: pronouns are magnets sticking to the sentence before. They can be two cats or books, not only people. This/these covered orally (this cake = the cake told about); split the beat if review requires.

options: It has bright yellow paint and a silver bell.
They were playing football in the field.
slides.answer: It has bright yellow paint and a silver bell.
slides.feedback: A fits: It is the bicycle from before. B fails: They needs more than one person.
slides.hint: Cover the gap. Read it in the last line. Which choice names that one thing?
slides.notes: PRACTISE Skill 2 (~6 min). Ask: who is He (Encik Hassan)? What is it (bicycle)? B-pickers match park/field place only: same place is not enough, the pronoun must match.

items: Result: So, Because, As a result.
slides.notes: MODEL Skill 3 (~7 min, choral repeat of 3 groups). Sayable: However turns, As a result continues to a result. Mini-check: it was raining, however... the next part must turn, not sunny. Counter: However and As a result point opposite ways; one must be wrong.

options: However, she forgot to set her alarm.
As a result, she passed with flying colours.
slides.answer: As a result, she passed with flying colours.
slides.feedback: B continues studied hard to top marks. A turns bad, fighting top marks.
slides.hint: Studied hard, then top marks. Turn or result?
slides.notes: PRACTISE Skill 3 (~6 min). Thumbs check: twist or result (result). A-pickers like the exam story: true in life, wrong here; the middle must lead up to top marks, not down.

items: Bridge: does it join before AND after?
Pronoun: who do he, she, it, they point to?
slides.notes: SYNTHESIS (~5 min, reference only, no new teaching, no pending answer). Choral read once, then finger match: Aina = 1, Hassan = 2, Mei Ling = 3. Sayable: good detectives use all three checks on every gap. Keep this card in mind for the two Master Challenges.

options: He found a tiny wet kitten crying under a leaf.
He quickly bought a cold bottle of juice.
slides.answer: He found a tiny wet kitten crying under a leaf.
slides.feedback: A names the kitten in the towel. B names juice, no animal.
slides.hint: Who is He? Which choice names the shivering animal needing a towel?
slides.notes: APPLY (~7 min: 2 min silent, 30 s whisper, reveal why). Withhold hint until after silent try. B-pickers take plausible life event: plausible is not enough, the after-sentence needs an animal. Ask which check helped most; accept bridge or pronoun.

options: So everyone put on sunglasses and sunblock.
However, a sudden storm hit an hour later.
slides.answer: However, a sudden storm hit an hour later.
slides.hint: Good start, bad end. Which word turns the story from sunny to stormy?
slides.notes: APPLY + EXIT EVIDENCE (~6 min: 2 min silent, reveal why, 1 min close). Scan fingers/boards; A-choosers match before only and need twist reteaching. Close sayable: bridge both sides, follow the pronoun, follow the signal. Next time: longer UASA gaps.
